cards.moa: α1 vasoconstriction with modest β1 inotropy; raises MAP with little rise in heart rate.
cards.dose: 0.01–1 mcg/kg/min via central line (start 0.05–0.1); titrate to MAP ≥65 mmHg.
cards.ci: Uncorrected hypovolaemia; peripheral extravasation causes necrosis (phentolamine).
cards.pearl: First-line vasopressor in septic and most other shock states.

cards.moa: V1-receptor vasoconstriction and restoration of vascular tone in vasodilatory shock.
cards.dose: 0.01–0.04 units/min fixed dose (do not titrate up beyond 0.04).
cards.ci: Mesenteric/digital ischaemia risk; caution in coronary disease.
cards.pearl: Add to norepinephrine as doses escalate (SSC 2021 used about 0.25–0.5 mcg/kg/min) to reduce catecholamine dose.

cards.moa: Low dose β effects (inotropy, chronotropy); high dose α-mediated vasoconstriction.
cards.dose: Infusion 0.01–0.5 mcg/kg/min; cardiac arrest 1 mg IV every 3–5 min; anaphylaxis 0.5 mg IM (1 mg/mL).
cards.ci: Arrhythmias; may raise lactate (β2-mediated) without hypoperfusion.
cards.pearl: Anaphylaxis: give IM first, early; refractory shock: second-line vasopressor.

cards.moa: Increases contractility and cardiac output with modest vasodilation.
cards.dose: 2.5–20 mcg/kg/min.
cards.ci: Hypertrophic obstruction, tachyarrhythmias, hypotension without vasopressor.
cards.pearl: Tachyphylaxis after 48–72 h; beta-blockers blunt response.

cards.moa: Raises cAMP: inotropy and vasodilation (inodilator) independent of β receptors.
cards.dose: 0.125–0.75 mcg/kg/min (bolus often omitted).
cards.ci: Hypotension, arrhythmias, severe obstructive disease.
cards.renal: Accumulates in renal impairment: reduce dose (e.g. 0.2–0.3 mcg/kg/min if CrCl <50).
cards.pearl: Preferred over dobutamine in patients on beta-blockers or with high pulmonary vascular resistance.

cards.moa: Dose-dependent: dopaminergic, then β1, then α1 effects.
cards.dose: 5–20 mcg/kg/min; no role for 'renal dose'.
cards.ci: Tachyarrhythmias, pheochromocytoma.
cards.pearl: Higher arrhythmia rates than norepinephrine in shock (SOAP II).

cards.moa: Rapid-onset, short-acting sedation; reduces cerebral metabolic rate.
cards.dose: Sedation 5–50 mcg/kg/min; induction 1–2 mg/kg.
cards.ci: Egg/soy hypersensitivity (relative); haemodynamic instability.
cards.pearl: Monitor triglycerides >48–72 h and watch for propofol infusion syndrome (acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, arrhythmia).

cards.moa: Central α2 agonism gives cooperative sedation with minimal respiratory depression.
cards.dose: 0.2–1.4 mcg/kg/h; loading doses are usually avoided.
cards.ci: Advanced heart block, hypovolaemia.
cards.renal: No adjustment (reduce in severe hepatic failure).
cards.pearl: Causes bradycardia and hypotension. PADIS 2025 suggests it over propofol in ventilated adults when light sedation or less delirium is the priority (conditional).

cards.moa: GABA-A positive allosteric modulation.
cards.dose: Sedation 0.02–0.1 mg/kg/h; status epilepticus 10 mg IM or 0.2 mg/kg IV.
cards.ci: Respiratory depression; avoid routine continuous infusion in ICU.
cards.renal: Active metabolites accumulate in renal failure.
cards.pearl: Prolonged infusions increase delirium and delay awakening.

cards.moa: Rapid onset, potent analgesia with haemodynamic stability.
cards.dose: 25–100 mcg bolus; infusion 25–200 mcg/h.
cards.ci: Respiratory depression; chest-wall rigidity at high bolus dose.
cards.pearl: First-line for analgosedation in the ventilated patient.

cards.moa: Dissociative anaesthesia with preserved airway reflexes and sympathetic stimulation.
cards.dose: Induction 1–2 mg/kg IV; analgesic 0.1–0.3 mg/kg; sedation infusion 0.5–2 mg/kg/h.
cards.ci: Severe hypertension, raised ICP historically (not contraindicated per recent data), psychosis.
cards.pearl: Good induction agent in shock; bronchodilation in severe asthma.

cards.moa: GABA-A modulator with minimal cardiovascular effect.
cards.dose: 0.3 mg/kg IV.
cards.ci: Adrenal suppression with repeated doses; sepsis controversies.
cards.pearl: Single dose induction is generally acceptable even in sepsis.

cards.moa: Competitive nicotinic receptor antagonist.
cards.dose: Induction 1.0–1.2 mg/kg; infusion 8–12 mcg/kg/min.
cards.ci: Anaphylaxis to NMBAs; prolonged weakness with steroids.
cards.pearl: Reversal with sugammadex 2–16 mg/kg.

cards.moa: Nicotinic agonist causing fasciculation then paralysis in 45–60 s.
cards.dose: 1.0–1.5 mg/kg IV.
cards.ci: Hyperkalaemia, burns >24 h, crush injury, denervation, malignant hyperthermia history.
cards.renal: Caution in renal failure with raised potassium.
cards.pearl: Raises potassium by about 0.5 mmol/L; fastest onset and offset.

cards.moa: Blocks potassium, sodium and calcium channels and has β-blocking effects.
cards.dose: VF/pVT arrest: 300 mg IV then 150 mg; infusion 1 mg/min for 6 h then 0.5 mg/min.
cards.ci: Bradycardia, QT prolongation, thyroid, pulmonary, hepatic toxicity.
cards.pearl: Phlebitis from peripheral infusion; use central access when possible.

cards.moa: Selective β1 blockade; half-life about 9 minutes.
cards.dose: Bolus 0.5 mg/kg then 50–300 mcg/kg/min.
cards.ci: Decompensated heart failure, bradycardia, heart block, severe asthma.
cards.pearl: Titratable rate control in aortic dissection and sepsis-related tachycardia (e.g. septic shock).

cards.moa: Releases nitric oxide, mainly venodilation at low dose.
cards.dose: 5–200 mcg/min; start 5–10 mcg/min.
cards.ci: PDE-5 inhibitor use, RV infarction, severe hypotension.
cards.pearl: Tolerance develops quickly; headache and hypotension common.

cards.moa: Inhibits NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb.
cards.dose: 20–80 mg IV bolus, or infusion 5–40 mg/h.
cards.ci: Anuria, hypovolaemia, hypokalaemia.
cards.renal: Higher doses needed in reduced GFR.
cards.pearl: Ototoxic at high infusion rates (>4 mg/min).

cards.moa: Potentiates antithrombin; inhibits factors IIa and Xa.
cards.dose: PE/ACS: 80 units/kg bolus then 18 units/kg/h, adjust to aPTT or anti-Xa.
cards.ci: Active bleeding, HIT.
cards.pearl: Reversal with protamine 1 mg per 100 units given in the last 2–3 hours.

cards.moa: Broad-spectrum activity against Gram-negatives, anaerobes and some Pseudomonas.
cards.dose: 4.5 g IV every 6–8 h (extended infusion over 3–4 h is common).
cards.ci: Penicillin allergy.
cards.pearl: Vancomycin combination increases AKI; use extended infusion for critically ill patients.

cards.moa: Inhibits cell-wall synthesis; broad Gram-negative and anaerobic coverage.
cards.dose: 1 g IV every 8 h (2 g every 8 h for CNS infections).
cards.ci: Carbapenem hypersensitivity.
cards.pearl: Lowers valproate levels; seizure risk less than imipenem.

cards.moa: Blocks cell-wall synthesis in Gram-positive organisms including MRSA.
cards.dose: Loading 20–35 mg/kg actual body weight; maintenance by AUC-guided dosing (AUC24 400–600).
cards.ci: Hypersensitivity; nephrotoxicity risk.
cards.pearl: Infuse slowly to avoid vancomycin infusion reaction (red man syndrome).

cards.moa: Replaces cortisol; enhances vascular responsiveness to catecholamines.
cards.dose: 50 mg IV every 6 h (or 200 mg/day infusion) in septic shock requiring ongoing vasopressors.
cards.ci: Uncontrolled infection without antibiotics; active GI bleeding caution.
cards.pearl: SSC 2026 suggests IV corticosteroids in septic shock; the 2021 criterion was norepinephrine ≥0.25 mcg/kg/min for ≥4 h (confirm in the 2026 text).

cards.q: A septic patient on norepinephrine 0.3 mcg/kg/min remains hypotensive. What is the guideline-supported next step?
o: Add vasopressin (up to 0.03 units/min) and consider hydrocortisone
cards.e: SSC suggests adding vasopressin when norepinephrine doses escalate (2021: about 0.25–0.5 mcg/kg/min) and IV corticosteroids for ongoing vasopressor requirement.

cards.q: Which sedative is least likely to cause respiratory depression?
cards.e: Dexmedetomidine is an α2 agonist that preserves respiratory drive, although it causes bradycardia and hypotension.
